'''Tie:''' {{legend0|#d2b1d9|40–50%}} {{legend0|#ae8bb1|50%}} {{legend0|#808080|No data}} | title = [[Governor of Texas|Governor]] | before_election = [[Rick Perry]] | before_party = Republican Party (United States) | after_election = [[Greg Abbott]] | after_party = Republican Party (United States) }} {{Elections in Texas sidebar}} The '''2014 Texas gubernatorial election''' was held on November 4, 2014, to elect the [[governor of Texas]]. Incumbent [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] governor [[Rick Perry]], who had served since the resignation of then-Governor [[George W. Bush]] on December 21, 2000, declined to run for an unprecedented fourth full term, making this the first [[open seat|open election]] for governor of the state since [[1990 Texas gubernatorial election|1990]]. The election took place between nominees who were selected on March 4, 2014: Republican [[Texas Attorney General|State Attorney General]] [[Greg Abbott]] and Democratic [[Texas Senate|State Senator]] [[Wendy Davis (politician)|Wendy Davis]]. Also on the ballot were [[Libertarian Party (United States)|Libertarian Party]] candidate Kathie Glass{{cite web | url=https://www.lptexas.org/texas-statewide-offices/84-candidates/1118-2014-statewide-offices-list | title=2014 Statewide Offices List | publisher=Libertarian Party of Texas | access-date=July 15, 2014 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140726081410/https://www.lptexas.org/texas-statewide-offices/84-candidates/1118-2014-statewide-offices-list | archive-date=July 26, 2014 | url-status=dead }} and [[Green Party (United States)|Green Party]] candidate Brandon Parmer.{{cite web|url=http://web.txgreens.org/|title=Green Party of Texas - Peace * Justice * Democracy * Ecology|access-date=October 11, 2014}} Abbott was projected to carry the election, and ultimately won handily with a 20.4 percentage point advantage.{{cite web|url=http://www.chron.com/news/houston-texas/houston/article/Polls-open-for-the-midterm-election-5868589.php|title=Up and down the ballot, a night of dominance for GOP in Texas and in Harris County|work=Houston Chronicle|date=November 5, 2014 |access-date=November 15, 2014}} As of 2022, this is the most recent gubernatorial election in which [[Bexar County, Texas|Bexar]], [[Harris County, Texas|Harris]] and [[Hays County, Texas|Hays]] counties voted Republican. Exit polls showed Abbott winning Whites (72% to 25%), while Davis received majorities among African Americans (92% to 7%) and Hispanics (55% to 44%). Abbott won roughly half of Hispanic men, 54% of all women, and 62% of married women.{{cite web|url=http://www.foxnews.com/politics/elections/2014/exit-polls?year=2014&type=governor&filter=TX|title=2014 Exit Polls - Politics - Fox News|work=Fox News|access-date=November 15, 2014}} Abbott
